result.title: Rethinking Perceptual Similarity for Remote Sensing: Multi-Layer Attention Scoring and Human Preference Benchmarking
result.comment: Accepted to the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027). 9 pages
result.summary: Perceptual similarity metrics for natural images transfer poorly to remote sensing (RS), where severe geospatial and semantic failures can remain visually plausible while still being decisively wrong for downstream use. To address this, we develop a novel human-aligned perceptual quality metric for generated RS imagery and evaluate it across several generation tasks. We first conduct a controlled perturbation study where we progressively increase the severity of common synthetic perturbations. Using the layer-wise Aligned Attention Score (AAS) responses in RemoteCLIP, we find that different RS artifacts are best captured at different depths. Based on these findings, we introduce Remote Sensing Perceptual Distance (RSPD), a pairwise metric that averages seven independently calibrated layer distances without tuning on human-preference labels. To evaluate our metric on realistic RS generation tasks, we construct a blind, reference-conditioned two-alternative forced-choice (2AFC) benchmark with five 300-triplet subsets spanning synthetic artifacts, airborne and spaceborne super-resolution, SAR-to-optical translation, and timeseries controls. We also construct a 300-triplet ordered misregistration benchmark with deterministic labels. Using the same RemoteCLIP checkpoint, RSPD substantially outperforms simple cosine distance with the final global embedding and is competitive with the strongest generic baselines across the realistic RS generation tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对遥感生成图像的感知相似度问题，先用逐级加重的合成扰动做控制实验，观察 RemoteCLIP 各层 Aligned Attention Score 的响应，发现不同伪影在浅层、深层被最好捕捉，据此提出不需在人类偏好标签上调参的七层平均距离 RSPD，并构建 2AFC 人类偏好基准与确定性配准误差基准来评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不同层最能反映不同视觉差异、按注意力对齐分数分层聚合」的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 与视觉特征相似度的深度选择、注意力结构影响提供可供核查的线索，但研究对象是生成图像质量评价而非推理过程本身。
